note: Independent instance-local HyperFrames component factories and helper modules. Scene mathematics and visual construction are adapted from the existing licensed source; no film player, shared scene registry or old engine clock is included. Component metadata owns fields, examples, action timing and sound hooks. DOM state, emoji, typography and scene context belong to each instance; the Three renderer/environment cache and ref-counted Metal shader pipeline are shared. Five additional community techniques are original native implementations following public motion references; their downloaded example compositions are research material and are not shipped. The optical glass implementation under glass/ is original project code ported from the user-approved local Three.js prototype (2026-11-22); it uses the existing pinned Three r170 dependency and its MIT provenance under ../vendor/three/. Island/lens retain their original fields.

sources.name: Comic Glitch Text (Pixel UI)
sources.license: MIT + Commons Clause + Attribution (Copyright (c) 2026 Kislay); ported and redistributed by the author's permission to Motion Fab, as the product owner states (2026-11-24)
sources.note: The comic scene (scenes/text.mjs). Kept from the original: 24 frames a second, the enter sequence (two glitches, chroma, a glitch, two chroma, ten bold, rest) and the idle re-glitch every 19 frames, the panel and shard polygons with their hatch, the red halftone patch, the three clipped ghost copies of a slice, the misregistration shadows and every colour. Changed for this engine: the frame comes from the scene's time and every random number from the word and the frame (the original runs a timer and Math.random), so a seek draws the same picture; no exit or loop; React and Tailwind classes became plain DOM and inline styles; the words' stagger follows the film's beat. The licence alone forbids ported versions and asks for a visible credit to https://pixelui.dev: the permission is the owner's to show, and the credit is his to place.
